summary: One native run of loader-diag-xnu-rx-md1 (decision 0030). The host streamed the 2,475,720,704-byte padded root image over USB bulk-OUT into the md1 reserve in 152.98 s (16.183 MB/s), 296 chunks, no error, no retry; the device and the loader both report committed == the whole image and loader status done. The payload kernel booted (16 KiB pages, md1 registered), PID 1 (the NAT-077 hash probe) read /dev/rmd1 and printed 11 digests covering the first 1,476,395,008 bytes (59.6%), every one equal to the host's SHA-256 of the same prefix; the kernel's timed return after 45 s cut the hash before the final line, so the digest of the whole image was not obtained. The phone ended in Download Mode at +382.39 s (cap-reset window), the pinned stock RECOVERY was restored with NAT-013 and Android was verified. Pre-registered row 3a: not a pass. The shipped analyser reports row 8 on the whole archive because the collector archive has two boots and the analyser takes the first; the same analyser on the second boot alone gives row 3a.

findings: Delivery works on the phone: 2,475,720,704 B in 152.98 s = 16.183 MB/s (host) and 152.97 s (loader clock), 296 TRBs, errors/dups/gaps/rejects/resets/aborts all 0. The 225 s budget needed 11.0 MB/s.
NAT-040 item U5 is answered for this controller: the DWC3 DMA writes into the reserve above 4 GiB (destination PA 0x902d7c000), directly.
The kernel read /dev/rmd1 through the MMU and matched the host for 11 consecutive prefix digests (1.375 GiB). The loader's final cache clean over the window was sufficient for that span.

The probe's SHA-256 (plain C, with the reads) runs at 33.0 MB/s; the whole image needs 75 s, the kernel's loader_return_after allows at most 63 s. Either a faster probe (SHA-256 instructions; read and hash timed separately) or the NAT-071 keepalive is needed for a whole-image digest.
The unpetted project kernel ran its 45 s and returned by itself; no SEC_UPLOAD.

The collector archive of this run has two boots: a capture-error (UsbTimeout, Errno 5) at 09:35:22Z, about when the kernel returned to the loader, and a new session at 09:35:37Z. Earlier runs (NAT-066, 068, 075) had one boot. The second boot holds the replay of the ring with the kernel text. The cause of the break is not established.

analyze_nat080.py takes the first boot of the image, so its output on the whole archive is row 8 ('no probe line'), which misdescribes the phone. This is a limitation of the analyser found by the real run, not a change of the pass rule; both outputs are kept.
pyusb set_configuration by the companion did not interrupt the collector: the loader's progress lines reached the host live (+41 s, +101 s, +181 s after the request for loader t=10 s, 70 s, 150 s).
established: native-device: a full-size (2.31 GiB) image can be placed into RAM over USB on this phone, with device-side checksum verification per chunk, in 153 s.
native-device: DWC3 DMA reaches the md1 reserve at PA 0x902d7c000 (above 4 GiB) without staging.
native-device: the kernel reads back the first 1,476,395,008 bytes of the delivered image through /dev/rmd1 unchanged (SHA-256 prefix digests equal to the host's).
native-device: the NAT-079 loader's receive cap, return path, pet schedule and the 360 s deadline reset worked as designed (Download Mode at +382.39 s).
not_established: The SHA-256 of the whole image as seen by the kernel; the last 999,325,696 bytes were not read back.
That APFS mounts from md1; that any Apple binary (dyld, launchd) runs; anything about display, input or GPU. The probe is not Apple's launchd.
The cause of the collector's break at the kernel's return.
Whether the 33 MB/s of the probe is limited by the read through mdevrw, by the SHA-256 code, or by the CPU clock the loader leaves.
